rows.note: This is the all-purpose spoken modifier for something that operates or exists in practice regardless of its official status.

example.english: This shop’s de facto opening hours are longer than those stated on the notice at the entrance.
example.traditional: 呢間舖實際上嘅營業時間，比門口張告示寫嘅長。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 pou3 sat6 zai3 soeng6 ge3 jing4 jip6 si4 gaan3 bei2 mun4 hau2 zoeng1 gou3 si6 se2 ge3 coeng4

rows.jyutping: sat6 zai3 zoeng2 kyun4 ge3 N
rows.note: Use this specifically for a person or organisation that is really in control despite not holding the official position.

example.english: Although Ming is not the chairperson, he is the de facto person in control of the committee.
example.traditional: 雖然阿明唔係主席，但佢係委員會入面實際掌權嘅人。
example.jyutping: seoi1 jin4 aa3 ming4 m4 hai6 zyu2 zik6 daan6 keoi5 hai6 wai2 jyun4 wui2 jap6 min6 sat6 zai3 zoeng2 kyun4 ge3 jan4

rows.note: Use this more formal or written alternative when stressing the contrast between the facts and the official or legal status.

example.english: Legally, Ms. Lee is not the head of the company, but she makes the de facto decisions for it.
example.traditional: 法律上李女士唔係公司負責人，但事實上嘅公司決策都由佢拍板。
